label: Interactive polish
tagline: Post-pass enrichment — microanimations, scroll/pointer effects, hover surprises, shader overlays — the orchestrator identifies WHERE; the drawers decide WHAT
description: The SEVENTH orchestrator sibling, with a DIFFERENT pipeline position. The other six run as the user's FIRST action (chat-Claude dispatches them up-front); this one runs LAST — after another primary orchestrator's build phase has completed (or after chat-Claude has hand-written source), AFTER any content/structure is in place, BEFORE Step-8 QA. Reads existing source HTML/CSS/JS + the committed genre/aesthetic, identifies SITES of opportunity for interactive enrichment, commits a polish register (subtle / playful / theatrical based on genre), and dispatches drawers per opportunity type. THE LOAD-BEARING DISCIPLINE: the orchestrator identifies WHERE + WHAT-TYPE of opportunity (microanimation / scroll-or-pointer-driven / hover-surprise / shader-overlay); the DRAWERS decide WHAT the specific improvement looks like (which microanimation, which shader effect, which hover reveal). Polish is a craft decision; if the orchestrator pre-decides, drawers become rubber-stampers and quality drops. Operates on the whole project — no slot tag, no per-slot fanout. Writes supplemental files to source/<branch>/_polish/<polishId>/ so existing source stays intact; the runtime drawer writes integration-instructions.md describing the minimal <link>/<script> edits the caller applies to each host page. Heavily co-dispatches visual-orchestrator with the shader skill for procedural overlays (halftone print, CRT scanlines, paper grain, glitch, dither). Drawers MAY be skipped — only the opportunity types research flagged dispatch. Pieces that are already richly interactive may commit siteCount=0 (a legitimate outcome).

triggers.title: Post-pass enrichment (LAST action before QA)
triggers.rule: After ANY primary orchestrator build phase completes (or after chat-Claude wrote source by hand via /prototype), BEFORE Step-8 QA, chat-Claude dispatches interactive-polish-orchestrator with project-wide scope. The orchestrator walks the resulting source, identifies enrichment sites per the genre, commits a polish pass. Also fires on explicit user request ('polish this' / 'make it feel more alive' / 'feels static'). One consistent flow — no mode branching.
